# Edit, abandon and restore changes and track mergeability

## Intent

A change lives longer than the push that opened it: its author rewords it, marks it ready, points it at another branch, gives it up and takes it back, and all the while the target branch moves under it. This package lets the people and agents who may modify a change do those things through the REST API and the `parley` CLI, and makes the hub tell them, without being asked, whether the change still applies to what it sits on, so that a conflict is known before anyone tries to land.

## Goals

- `PATCH /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number` edits `title`, `intent`, `labels`, `auto_land`, `state` (`draft` ⇄ `open`) and `target_branch`, for the author, for anyone with write access to the target workspace and for the admin token, and for nobody else.
- `POST …/abandon` abandons a change, with an explicit choice for its dependants; `POST …/restore` brings an abandoned change back to `open` at its last version, recreating a deleted source branch.
- A landed change accepts only a change of `labels`; an abandoned change accepts no edit.
- Every `draft` or `open` change carries `mergeable` (`clean`, `conflict` or `unknown`) for its current head against the current head of what it sits on, recomputed in the background after every new version and every move of the target branch, coalesced per change and spaced by `[changes].mergeable_debounce`.
- A change that starts to conflict gets a stored conflict report and one `parley.change.conflict` event; a change that becomes landable gets one `parley.change.ready` event.
- After a crash between a ref update and its bookkeeping, the next start records the missed head as a version.
- `parley change edit|ready|draft|abandon|restore|wait` drive the routes and wait for a change to be landed, ready or mergeable.

## Requirements

### Who may modify a change

`PATCH`, abandon and restore need `changes:write` for a PAT (`403 insufficient_scope` otherwise, whether or not the workspace exists) and read access to the target workspace (`404 not_found`, "workspace not found", otherwise). A number that names no change of the workspace answers `404`, `error_type: change_not_found`. For a token bound to a fork F used on F's parent, a change whose source workspace is not F also answers `404 change_not_found` (CHG-FR-040).

Among the callers who can read the change, three may modify it (CHG-FR-020): the author, meaning the user whose id is `author.actor_id`, with any credential of that user; anyone with write access to the target workspace; and the admin token. Every other reader gets `403 forbidden` and the change is unchanged. This is what lets an org member who has only read access to a workspace edit the change they opened from their fork.

After that the target workspace's status is checked (WS-FR-007): `pending`, `cloning` or a running reclone, archive or delete answers `409 workspace_busy`; `failed` answers `409 workspace_not_ready`; `archived` answers `409 workspace_archived`.

### Editing title, intent, labels and auto_land

`PATCH /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number` takes any of `title`, `intent`, `labels`, `auto_land`, `state` and `target_branch`. It answers `200` with the change object. Members that are absent keep their value; `labels` replaces the whole list. All members of one request are applied together or not at all.

- `title`: 1 to 200 characters, no line break. `intent`: at most 16,000 characters. `labels`: at most 20 after duplicates are removed, each matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.:/-]{0,62}$`. A wrong JSON type, a `state` other than `draft` or `open`, or a value outside these limits is `400 invalid_request`.
- The intent may be empty only while the change is `draft` or when the workspace setting `changes.require_intent` is false. A request whose result would be an `open` change with an empty intent under `require_intent: true` is `400`, `error_type: intent_required`.
- `auto_land: true` stores the flag and the calling user as the one who set it, with the credential type and the token's `paths` globs (LAND-FR-060 checks that user later); `false` clears them. A `PATCH` whose body has an `auto_land` member asks the registered `auto_land` guard first, with the caller, the change and the value, before any member of the request is applied; when the guard refuses (`403 path_not_allowed` with the path, for a path-scoped token) the whole request is refused and nothing changes.
- An abandoned change answers `409`, `error_type: change_closed`, to every edit. A landed change answers `409 change_closed` when the body has any of these members other than `labels`, and accepts `labels` alone (CHG-FR-024).
- A body with none of the members changes nothing and answers `200` with `updated_at` unchanged.

### Draft and open

`state: "open"` on a draft moves it to `open` when the title and intent rules hold, re-evaluates `landing` (the structural reason `draft` goes away) and emits `parley.change.open` with `was_draft: true`, `title`, `target_branch`, `source_workspace`, `source_branch` and `depends_on`. `state: "draft"` on an open change moves it to `draft`; its `landing.status` becomes `blocked` with reason `draft`; no event is emitted. Asking for the state the change already has changes nothing.

### Retargeting

`target_branch` on a `draft` or `open` change that has no `depends_on` and no dependants moves the change to another branch of the same workspace (CHG-FR-021). The new target passes the target rules of opening (CHG-FR-003, CHG-FR-005): it exists (`400 target_not_found`), it is not the change's own source branch (`400 invalid_request`), and it is not a carry-patch integration branch (`403 integration_branch`). A change in a stack answers `409 conflict`.

A retarget creates no version. It sets `base_sha` to the merge base of the head with the new target and recomputes `stats` and `paths`, re-evaluates `landing`, sets `mergeable` to `unknown`, schedules the check, and emits `parley.change.version` with `kind: "retarget"`. When the new target already contains every commit of the change, or a merge commit lies between the new target and the head, the retarget is still accepted and `landing.status` is `blocked` with reason `nothing_to_land` or `merge_commits` (§7.10). A change whose target branch was deleted can be retargeted. Naming the current target changes nothing.

### Abandon

`POST …/abandon` with `{"reason"?: string, "dependants"?: "reparent" | "abandon"}` (or no body) moves a `draft` or `open` change to `abandoned`, answers `200` with the change object and emits `parley.change.abandon` with `reason`. It never deletes the source branch or a version (CHG-FR-022). An abandoned or landed change answers `409 change_closed`. A `dependants` value other than the two, or a `reason` that is not a string, is `400 invalid_request`.

A change with dependants needs the choice: without `dependants` the answer is `409`, `error_type: has_dependants`, and nothing changes. With `abandon`, every change above it in the stack is abandoned in the same step, each with its own event. With `reparent`, each direct dependant's `depends_on` becomes the abandoned change's own `depends_on` (or null), and the hub asks, in the same transaction, for a restack of each with trigger `abandon`, so that it no longer holds the abandoned change's commits. The restack itself is package 24's.

### Restore

`POST …/restore` moves an abandoned change to `open` at its last version, answers `200` with the change object and emits `parley.change.restore` (CHG-FR-023). `landing` is re-evaluated, `mergeable` is `unknown` and a check is scheduled. If the source branch no longer exists it is recreated at the last version's head.

Refusals, in this order: the change is not abandoned (`409`, `error_type: change_not_abandoned`); the source workspace no longer exists (`409`, `error_type: source_workspace_gone`; the versions stay fetchable); another `draft` or `open` change uses the source branch (`409 change_exists`); the source branch is gone and the last version's commit is gone too, as after a reclone (`409 conflict`); the intent is empty while `changes.require_intent` is true (`400 intent_required`).

### Mergeability

`mergeable` answers whether the current version's own commits (`base_sha` to `head_sha`) would rebase cleanly onto the current head of the target branch, or, for a change whose `depends_on` names a `draft` or `open` change, onto the current head of that change (§7.3.4). The hub finds out with a trial rebase that writes no ref.

It is recomputed after every new version (a `restack` version of package 24 included), after every move of a target branch that has `draft` or `open` changes, after a new version of the change below, after a retarget and after a restore. A restack therefore needs no rule of its own: the version it records sets `mergeable` to `unknown` and the check runs for the new head against the head it now sits on. When a restack fails with a conflict, package 24 stores `conflict` and the report through this package's storing function, for the pair of the change's head and the commit it was replayed onto; when package 24 clears `needs_restack` without a new version, it calls this package's trigger and the value is computed again. Until the result for the new pair of commits is stored the value is `unknown`. Checks of one change coalesce: only the latest pair is computed, and a result for a pair that is no longer current is thrown away. Computations of one change start at least `[changes].mergeable_debounce` apart (default `5s`; `0s` means no spacing; a negative or unparsable value stops `parleyd` at start with a configuration error naming the key).

When the target branch does not exist, `mergeable` stays `unknown` and `landing.status` becomes `blocked` with reason `target_not_found`. When the trial rebase fails for another reason than a conflict, or runs longer than 30 seconds, `mergeable` stays `unknown`, the failure is logged and the next trigger tries again.

### Conflict and ready events

When a computation finds a conflict and the last computed value was not `conflict`, the hub stores the conflict report (the type `ConflictReport` of `internal/gitrepo`, declared by package 20) on the change and emits `parley.change.conflict` with `files` (the conflicted paths) and `needs_restack`. While the change stays in conflict, across versions, the report is replaced and no further event is emitted. A computation that finds `clean` clears the report.

A change is landable when it is `open`, its `landing.status` is `ready` and its `mergeable` is `clean`. When a change becomes landable for a head it has not been announced for, the hub emits one `parley.change.ready` (actor `system`). The announcement is forgotten when the change stops being landable with a computed `mergeable`, and when it is retargeted; a target move that leaves the change `clean` emits nothing. The announcement runs after each mergeability result and after each edit of this package that re-evaluates `landing`. It is one exported function, `AnnounceLandable` in `internal/change/landable.go`, and the only writer of `parley.change.ready`: package 27 runs it in every transaction in which it stores a `landing`, and no other package writes the event.

Every event of this package has `resource_type: "change"`, the change number as `resource_id`, the target workspace, the session when known, and `number`, `ref`, `version` and `head_sha` in its metadata. An event and the state change it reports are written together.

### Start-up reconciliation

Before `parleyd` accepts requests it compares, for every `draft` or `open` change, the head of the current version with the head of the source branch. A differing head is recorded as a new version, with everything a new version brings (CHG-FR-011). A missing source branch abandons the change with reason `source_deleted`. Every `draft` or `open` change whose `mergeable` is `unknown` gets a check scheduled. A change that cannot be reconciled is logged and skipped; the start goes on.

### CLI

- `parley change edit <slug> <number>` with `--title`, `--intent` (text, `@file`, or `-` for stdin), `--label` and `--remove-label` (repeatable), `--auto-land` or `--no-auto-land`, `--target`: sends one `PATCH` with the members the flags name. With label flags it first reads the change and sends the resulting list.
- `parley change ready <slug> <number>` and `parley change draft <slug> <number>` send `PATCH` with `{"state":"open"}` and `{"state":"draft"}`.
- `parley change abandon <slug> <number>` with `--reason` and `--dependants reparent|abandon`; `parley change restore <slug> <number>`.
- `parley change wait <slug> <number>` with `--for landed|ready|mergeable` (default `landed`), `--timeout` (default `5m`) and `--poll-interval` (default `5s`): polls the change. Exit 0 with the change on stdout when the condition holds; exit 1 with `wait_failed` and the change on stdout when it can no longer hold; exit 1 with `wait_timeout` and nothing on stdout on timeout.

Each command prints the route's response and exits by the rules of PLAT-FR-092 and PLAT-FR-093. `edit` without an edit flag, a flag together with its `--no-` form, an unknown `--for` or `--dependants` value, and a `--timeout` or `--poll-interval` that is not positive are usage errors (exit 2) and send no request.

### End-to-end flows

1. An agent opens a draft from its fork, runs `parley change edit` to set the intent and `parley change ready`; `parleyd` moves the change to `open`, emits `parley.change.open`, computes `mergeable: clean` in the background and emits `parley.change.ready`; `parley change wait --for ready` exits 0.
2. A developer's push moves the target branch so that an open change no longer applies; `parleyd` recomputes, stores the conflict report and emits one `parley.change.conflict`; the agent pushes a fixed version; `parleyd` computes `clean` and clears the report.
3. A developer abandons a change, deletes its source branch with git and restores the change; `parleyd` recreates the branch at the last version's head and the change is `open` again.
4. An operator restarts `parleyd` after a source branch moved without its bookkeeping; `parleyd` records the missed head as a version before it serves requests.

## Design Decisions

1. Language Go; git operations run the `git` binary through `internal/gitrepo`; no git library. The trial rebase is the one `internal/gitrepo` offers to the compare route of package 20. (Project decisions 1 and 6.)
2. State is in the embedded SQLite store behind `internal/store`; an event is written in the same transaction as its state change through `internal/event`. (Project decision 2.)
3. HTTP uses `net/http`; the CLI uses `github.com/spf13/cobra`; tests use `testing`, `httptest` and repositories made with `git init` in `t.TempDir()`. (Project decisions 3, 4 and 7.)
4. `depends_on` in the `PATCH` body is package 24's. This package hands a present member to `SetDependsOn` of the `StackLinker` interface that package 22 declares and package 24 implements, inside the `PATCH` transaction, and specifies nothing about it: its validation (`400 invalid_dependency`), its effect and its restack are in package 24. While no stack linker is registered the member is ignored like any unknown member (PLAT-FR-017). Why: the plan gives `depends_on` to package 24, which depends on this one.
5. The restack of reparented dependants is done by a restack collaborator that package 24 supplies. This package declares the interface `Restacker` in `internal/change/lifecycle.go` (request the restack of one change with a trigger name, inside a store transaction) and calls it inside the abandon's transaction, after it has relinked the dependants itself; while none is registered, abandon relinks the dependants, sets their `mergeable` to `unknown` and schedules their check. Why: this package cannot depend on package 24, and package 24 writes its pending restack in the transaction of the event that caused it.
6. `dependants=abandon` abandons the whole stack above, not only the direct dependants, each with the request's `reason`. Why: a change left depending on an abandoned change has nothing to sit on.
7. The `reason` of an abandon is stored and emitted as given; absent, it is the empty string. `dependants` on a change with no dependants is accepted and has no effect. Why: the PRD names no default and no limit other than the body size.
8. A retarget of a change that is in a stack answers `409 conflict`. Why: the PRD forbids it and names no specific type.
9. Restoring a change whose source branch and last version's commit are both gone answers `409 conflict`. Why: §7.10 says it cannot be restored and names no type.
10. Restoring a change with an empty intent under `changes.require_intent: true` answers `400 intent_required`. Why: restore moves to `open`, and an open change may not have an empty intent; a new change can be opened from the branch.
11. Restoring a change whose source branch exists at a head other than the last version's records that head as a new version of kind `ref`, created by the restoring caller. Why: an open change's current version is always the head of its source branch, and `ref` is the kind of every version recorded for a head that was already on the source branch (decision 23 of package 22: a REST open, a restore, start-up reconciliation).
12. A version recorded by start-up reconciliation has kind `ref` and `created_by.actor_type` `system`, with no creating credential. Why: the original cause is unknown after a crash, and the rule of decision 11 applies. This is also what closes the gap the ref writer of package 18 leaves when the hub stops between its ref commit and its store commit.
13. Start-up reconciliation abandons a `draft` or `open` change whose source branch is missing, with reason `source_deleted` and actor `system`. Why: it is the bookkeeping of CHG-FR-013 that a crash lost.
14. Start-up reconciliation finishes before the listener accepts requests, and schedules a check for every change left `unknown`. Why: no push can race it, and mergeability checks are not durable.
15. Transitions are judged against the last computed value; `unknown` in between does not count. `parley.change.conflict` is therefore not repeated for a new version that still conflicts (§14.8: "not repeated while it stays so"), and `parley.change.ready` is emitted once per head and landable period, not after every target move.
16. A failed or timed-out trial rebase (30 seconds, the read deadline of §6) leaves `mergeable` at `unknown` and is not retried on a timer. Why: the next version or target move triggers it again; the PRD defines no retry.
17. `[changes].mergeable_debounce` accepts `0s`; a negative or unparsable value is a configuration error at start.
18. A `PATCH` with none of the editable members answers `200` and changes nothing, `updated_at` included. Editing `title`, `intent`, `labels` or `auto_land` emits no event. Duplicate labels are removed, keeping the first occurrence, before the limit of 20 is applied.
19. The three write routes apply the workspace status answers of WS-FR-007 to the target workspace.
20. `parley change wait`: `--for ready` holds when `landing.status` is `ready` and `mergeable` is `clean`, and fails on `landing.status: blocked` or `mergeable: conflict`; `--for mergeable` holds on `mergeable: clean` and fails on `conflict` only. An abandoned change fails every wait; a landed change ends every wait with exit 0. Why: the PRD's sentence about `blocked` and `conflict` is read per condition, since a draft is always `blocked`.
21. `parley change edit --intent` takes the same three forms as `parley change open --intent`.
22. Triggers come from two registrations (with packages 18 and 22): a version observer of package 22 for every new version, and a ref-updated stage of package 18's ref writer for target branches moved by a push, an API write or a land; a sync reaches this package through the branch-move observer of package 12. Why: those are the places where the hub learns of the move inside the transaction that makes it.
23. One function stores a mergeability result with its conflict report and the `parley.change.conflict` event, and package 24 uses it for a restack conflict (with package 24). Why: two writers of `mergeable` and of the event would announce one conflict twice.
24. Abandon and restore of a change whose source is a fork report fork activity through the `ForkActivity` interface of package 22 (with package 16): abandon through package 22's move to `abandoned`, restore by a call of its own. A landing is reported by package 16's own after-landing hook in package 25.
25. `AnnounceLandable` is the single writer of `parley.change.ready` (with packages 27 and 29). It takes the store transaction and the change (workspace and number), writes the event and remembers the announced head, or forgets the announcement, as REQ-8 says, and does nothing while `mergeable` is `unknown`. Package 27 calls it in every transaction that stores a `landing`; package 29 starts automatic lands from the event alone. Why: the condition has two inputs with two owners, and one writer that remembers the announced head gives one event per transition.
26. `PATCH` asks the `auto_land` guard before it applies anything (with packages 22 and 29). The guard is the `AutoLandGuard` that package 22 declares in `internal/change/collaborators.go` and package 29 registers. It is called inside the `PATCH` transaction, after validation and the state rules and before the first member is written, for every body that has an `auto_land` member, with the caller (user and credential), the change and the value; a refusal is answered unchanged and rolls the request back. Only `true` can be refused; the call for `false` lets package 29 drop what it keeps about the flag. Without a registered guard the flag is stored as given. The flag has one store: this package extends `SetAutoLand(tx, change, value, caller)` of `internal/change`, through which the `Open` of package 22 and this `PATCH` both write the flag, to store the setter beside it (the user's id, the credential type and the token's `paths` globs or null) and exposes the accessor `AutoLandSetter(tx, change)`; package 29 keeps no setter row of its own and reads the accessor.
27. Wiring is in `internal/hub/change.go`: the routes, the worker's start and stop, the observer and stage registrations and the start-up reconciliation are registered there, beside package 22's.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task. It shares history with the parent, has its own branches and expires: after 7 days by default, or 24 hours after all its changes have landed or been abandoned.
- **Change**: The unit of work: a proposal to add the commits of a source branch to a target branch, with a number, a title, an intent, versions and a state.
- **Version**: One head of a change's source branch. Every push, API commit or restack that moves the source creates a new version. Old versions stay fetchable.
- **Intent**: The author's statement of why the change exists.
- **Stack**: Changes linked by `depends_on`, lowest first.
- **Restack**: The hub rebasing a dependent change onto the new head of the change below it, or onto the target once that change has landed.
- **Landing**: Adding a change's commits to its target branch: a server-side rebase followed by a compare-and-swap of the target ref.
- **Conflict report**: The structured description of why a rebase could not be done: files, kinds, and the landed changes involved.
- **Policy**: A workspace's ordered rules that map touched paths to landing requirements.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it). A token bound to a fork also reaches its own changes, and the awareness and policy reads, on the fork's parent (§3).
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number. Hub events form the audit log and the event stream.
- **Landable**: An `open` change whose `landing.status` is `ready` and whose `mergeable` is `clean`.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Who may modify a change

**Rationale:** An org member must be able to edit the change they opened into a workspace they can only read, and nobody else who can merely read it may touch it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN PATCH /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number, POST …/abandon or POST …/restore is called by the user whose id is the change's author.actor_id with any credential of that user, by a caller with write access to the target workspace, or with the admin token, THE parleyd SHALL pass the request on to the validation and state checks of the route
   → the route answers with its own result (HTTP 200 for a valid request), never 403 forbidden
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: change demo#1 opened by mia from demo--t1 into main; a second, abandoned change demo#2 by mia for the restore rows
   ```
   in internal/change/authz_test.go, a table over callers {mia's API key (author, member access only); mia's PAT with changes:write; owner's API key (not the author); the admin token} x routes {PATCH with {"labels":["x"]}; POST abandon; POST restore on an abandoned change}: r = call(route, caller); assert r.status == 200
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF one of the three routes is called by a caller who can read the target workspace and is neither the change's author, nor a caller with write access to the target workspace, nor the admin token, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and leave the change unchanged
   → HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden; a following GET of the change returns the same body as before the call
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: change demo#1 opened by mia; a second org member 'noa' with an API key
   ```
   in internal/change/authz_test.go beside the table above, over the three routes with the API key of 'noa', a second org member who did not open the change: before = get(change); r = call(route, noaKey); assert r.status == 403 and r.json.error.error_type == 'forbidden'; assert get(change) == before; assert no parley.change.* event was written
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF one of the three routes is called with a PAT that lacks the scope changes:write, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request before looking at the workspace or the change
   → HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope, with the same body for an existing workspace and for a slug that names no workspace
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: change demo#1
   ```
   in internal/change/authz_test.go: pat = owner's PAT with only changes:read; for each of the three routes: a = call(route on 'demo', pat); b = call(route on 'nope', pat); assert a.status == 403 and a.json.error.error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert a.body == b.body
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF one of the three routes names a number that no change of the workspace has, a :number that is not a positive decimal integer, or, for a caller whose token is bound to fork F and who addresses F's parent, a change whose source workspace is not F, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without revealing whether the change exists
   → HTTP 404 with error_type change_not_found; the three cases have the same status and error_type
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: change demo#1 from demo--t1; change demo#3 opened by owner from a branch of demo itself; a PAT of mia bound to demo--t1 with changes:write
   ```
   in internal/change/authz_test.go, a table over {number 999; number 'abc'; number '0'; mia's token bound to demo--t1 addressing demo#3 whose source workspace is demo} x the three routes: r = call(route); assert r.status == 404 and r.json.error.error_type == 'change_not_found'; then with the same bound token on demo#1 (source demo--t1): assert PATCH {"labels":["x"]} answers 200
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF one of the three routes is called by a caller who has no read access to the target workspace, THEN THE parleyd SHALL answer as for a workspace that does not exist
   → HTTP 404 with error_type not_found and the same body as the same route on a slug that names no workspace
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: change demo#1 opened by mia
   ```
   in internal/change/authz_test.go: outsider = a user outside the organization; a = call(PATCH demo#1, outsiderKey); b = call(PATCH nope#1, outsiderKey); assert a.status == 404 and a.json.error.error_type == 'not_found'; assert a.body == b.body; then remove mia from the organization and assert mia's PATCH of her own demo#1 answers the same 404
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] IF one of the three routes passes the caller rule and the body validation while the target workspace's status is pending, cloning, failed or archived, or a reclone, archive or delete of it is running, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and leave the change unchanged
   → HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy (pending, cloning, running maintenance), workspace_not_ready (failed) or workspace_archived (archived)
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: change demo#1 (open) and demo#2 (abandoned)
   ```
   in internal/change/authz_test.go, a table over workspace status {pending -> workspace_busy; cloning -> workspace_busy; failed -> workspace_not_ready; archived -> workspace_archived} x the three routes, called with the admin token: set the status on the workspace record; r = call(route); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.error_type == want; assert the change's state and updated_at are unchanged
   ```

### REQ-2: Edit title, intent, labels and auto_land

**Rationale:** The intent travels with the change, so its author must be able to state and correct it after opening.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN PATCH /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number is called on a draft or open change with a body holding any of title, intent, labels and auto_land, each within its limits, THE parleyd SHALL store the named members together, keep every member that is absent from the body, replace the whole labels list with the given one after removing duplicates (first occurrence kept), advance updated_at and write no event
   → HTTP 200 with the change object carrying the new values; a following GET returns the same object
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: open change demo#1 with title 'T', intent 'i', labels ['old'], auto_land false
   ```
   in internal/change/edit_test.go, a table over bodies {only title 'T2'; only intent 'why'; labels ['a','b','a'] -> ['a','b']; labels [] ; title of exactly 200 characters; intent of exactly 16000 characters; 20 distinct labels; a label of 63 characters 'a' + 62 x '.'; title and labels together; a body with an extra unknown member 'foo'}: before = get(change); r = patch(body); assert r.status == 200; assert the named members equal the wanted values and every other member except updated_at equals before; assert get(change) == r.json; assert the event log has no new event
   ```

[REQ-2.2] IF the PATCH body holds a title that is empty, longer than 200 characters or contains a line feed or carriage return, an intent longer than 16,000 characters, more than 20 distinct labels, a label that does not match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.:/-]{0,62}$, a state other than "draft" or "open", or a member of the wrong JSON type, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the whole request and apply none of its members, including the valid ones

### REQ-3: Move a change between draft and open

**Rationale:** A draft is work nobody should land or review yet; marking it ready is the moment reviewers and automation are told.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a PATCH with state "open" addresses a draft whose resulting title and intent satisfy the title and intent rules, THE parleyd SHALL move the change to open, re-evaluate its landing so that the structural reason draft no longer applies, and write one parley.change.open event in the same transaction
   → HTTP 200 with state open and landing.reason not 'draft'; one event parley.change.open with actor the caller, resource_type change, resource_id the number, and metadata number, ref, version, head_sha, title, target_branch, source_workspace, source_branch, depends_on and was_draft true
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: draft change demo#1 by mia with a title and a non-empty intent; no policy set on the workspace
   ```
   in internal/change/edit_test.go: r = patch(draft, {state:'open'}, miaKey); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.state == 'open' and r.json.landing.reason != 'draft' and r.json.landing.status == 'ready' (default policy); ev = the events of type parley.change.open for the change; assert len(ev) == 1 and ev[0].actor_id == mia.id and ev[0].workspace == 'demo' and ev[0].resource_id == '1' and ev[0].metadata includes {number:1, ref:'demo#1', version:1, head_sha:<head>, title, target_branch:'main', source_workspace:'demo--t1', source_branch, depends_on:null, was_draft:true}
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN a PATCH with state "draft" addresses an open change, THE parleyd SHALL move the change to draft, re-evaluate its landing, keep its versions, labels, auto_land flag and mergeable value, and write no event
   → HTTP 200 with state draft and landing {status: 'blocked', reason: 'draft'}; the event log has no new event
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: open change demo#1 with auto_land true and mergeable clean
   ```
   in internal/change/edit_test.go: before = get(open change); r = patch({state:'draft'}); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.state == 'draft' and r.json.landing.status == 'blocked' and r.json.landing.reason == 'draft'; assert r.json.version == before.version and r.json.mergeable == before.mergeable and r.json.auto_land == before.auto_land; assert no new event
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHEN a PATCH names the state the change already has and no other editable member, THE parleyd SHALL change nothing and write no event
   → HTTP 200 with the change object equal to the object before the call, updated_at included
   Check: integration
   ```
   in internal/change/edit_test.go, a table {open change, {state:'open'}; draft, {state:'draft'}}: before = get(change); r = patch(body); assert r.status == 200 and r.json == before; assert no parley.change.open event was written
   ```

### REQ-4: Retarget a change

**Rationale:** A change opened against the wrong branch, or one whose target was deleted, must be movable without losing its number, versions and approvals history.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a PATCH names a target_branch that differs from the current one, on a draft or open change that has no depends_on and no dependants, and the branch passes the target rules of opening, THE parleyd SHALL set target_branch, set base_sha to the merge base of head_sha with the new target's head, recompute stats and paths against it, create no version, re-evaluate landing, set mergeable to unknown, schedule the mergeability check, forget the ready announcement, and write one parley.change.version event with kind retarget in the same transaction
   → HTTP 200 with the new target_branch, base_sha, stats and paths, the same version number and head_sha, and mergeable 'unknown'; GET …/versions lists the same versions as before; one event parley.change.version with actor the caller and metadata number, ref, version, head_sha, kind 'retarget', base_sha, patch_equivalent_to null and draft
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: branches main and release in demo; open change demo#1 from a branch of demo--t1 into main
   ```
   in internal/change/edit_test.go: main and release diverge by one commit each; the change has one commit on top of main touching a.txt; versionsBefore = get(versions); r = patch({target_branch:'release'}); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.target_branch == 'release' and r.json.base_sha == git merge-base(head, release) and r.json.version == 1 and r.json.head_sha == head and r.json.mergeable == 'unknown'; assert r.json.stats.commits == count(release..head) and r.json.paths == files of base_sha..head; assert get(versions) == versionsBefore; ev = events parley.change.version after the call; assert len(ev) == 1 and ev[0].metadata.kind == 'retarget' and ev[0].metadata.base_sha == r.json.base_sha and ev[0].metadata.draft == false; wait until get(change).mergeable != 'unknown'
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] IF the named target_branch does not exist in the workspace, is the change's own source branch in the same workspace, or is the integration branch of a carry-patch workspace, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the whole request with the answer opening a change gives for the same target, and leave the change unchanged
   → HTTP 400 with error_type target_not_found (missing branch); HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request (own source branch); HTTP 403 with error_type integration_branch (integration branch); no event is written
   Check: integration

### REQ-5: Abandon a change

**Rationale:** Work that will not land must leave the list of open work without losing what was pushed.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN POST /workspaces/:slug/changes/:number/abandon is called on a draft or open change that has no dependants, with no body, an empty object, or a body with a string reason, THE parleyd SHALL move the change to abandoned, drop its pending mergeability check, leave its source branch and every version ref in place, and write one parley.change.abandon event in the same transaction
   → HTTP 200 with state abandoned; the source branch still resolves to the same commit and refs/parley/changes/<number>/<version> still resolves for every version; one event parley.change.abandon with actor the caller and metadata number, ref, version, head_sha and reason (the given string, or the empty string when absent)
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: one change per row with one version
   ```

### REQ-7: Compute mergeability in the background

**Rationale:** An agent should learn that its change stopped applying when the target moves, not when someone tries to land it.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN a mergeability check runs for a draft or open change, THE parleyd SHALL trial-rebase the current version's own commits (base_sha to head_sha) onto the current head of the target branch, or onto the current head of the change named by depends_on when that change is draft or open, and store clean or conflict on the change together with the pair of commits it was computed for
   → GET of the change returns mergeable 'clean' when the commits apply and 'conflict' with a non-null conflict report when they do not; a draft is computed like an open change
   Check: integration
   - setup: a workspace 'demo' with a real bare repository made with git in t.TempDir()
   - setup: the change store and the mergeability worker with debounce 0s, driven directly without HTTP for the scheduling
   ```
   in internal/change/mergeable_test.go, a table {change touching a.txt, target advanced by a commit touching b.txt -> clean; change editing line 1 of a.txt, target advanced by a commit editing line 1 of a.txt -> conflict with conflict.files[0].path == 'a.txt'; the same two rows for a draft; a change demo#2 with depends_on 1 whose commits apply to demo#1's head but conflict with main's head -> clean; demo#2 with depends_on 1 after demo#1 got a new head that edits the same line -> conflict; demo#2 whose depends_on names an abandoned change -> computed against main's head}: run the check to completion; c = get(change); assert c.mergeable == want; assert (c.conflict != null) == (want == 'conflict')
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] WHEN a version is recorded for a draft or open change, a branch that is the target of draft or open changes moves, a draft or open change that other draft or open changes depend on gets a new version, a change is retargeted, or a change is restored, THE parleyd SHALL set mergeable to unknown on each affected change no later than the triggering transaction commits, and schedule one check per affected change
   → the triggers arrive through the version observer of package 22 (every new version, a restack version of package 24 included) and the ref-updated stage this package registers with the ref writer of package 18 (target moves by push, API write and land); between the trigger and the stored result GET returns mergeable 'unknown'; afterwards it returns 'clean' or 'conflict' for the new pair of commits without any further request
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: changes demo#1 and demo#3 into main, demo#2 depending on demo#1, demo#4 into release, all with mergeable clean
   ```
   in internal/change/mergeable_test.go, with the worker paused by a test gate, a table over triggers {push of a second commit to the source branch -> that change; push to main (target of demo#1 and demo#3, not of demo#4 which targets release) -> demo#1 and demo#3 unknown, demo#4 untouched; new version of demo#1 while demo#2 depends on it -> demo#1 and demo#2; retarget of demo#4 -> demo#4; restore of an abandoned change -> that change}: fire the trigger through the real route or a real git push; assert get(each affected change).mergeable == 'unknown' and each unaffected change keeps its value; open the gate; assert each affected change reaches 'clean' or 'conflict' within the test deadline; assert a move of a branch that is the target of no draft or open change schedules nothing
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any sequence of triggers that arrive for one change while a check of that change is waiting or running, compute only the pair of commits that is current when a computation starts, and discard a result whose pair of commits is no longer the change's current head and onto-commit when it would be stored
   → after ten target moves in a burst, at most two trial rebases ran for the change and the stored result is the one for the last target head; a result for a superseded pair never appears in GET
   Check: integration
   - setup: the mergeability worker with debounce 0s and a real repository
   ```
   in internal/change/mergeable_test.go, with a counting wrapper around the trial rebase and a gate that holds the first computation: trigger once and let the computation start; move main ten times, the last move making the change conflict; assert get(change).mergeable == 'unknown' throughout; release the gate; wait for a stored result; assert get(change).mergeable == 'conflict' and get(change).conflict.target_sha == the last head of main; assert the wrapper counted at most 2 trial rebases for the change
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] WHILE [changes].mergeable_debounce is a positive duration d (default 5s), THE parleyd SHALL start two computations of the same change at least d apart, computing a trigger that arrives inside the interval when the interval ends, and never delay one change because of another change's interval

### REQ-8: Announce conflicts and landable changes

**Rationale:** Agents and automatic landing follow the event stream; each must hear once that a change broke and once that it can land.

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN a computation finds a conflict for a change whose last computed mergeable value was clean or that has no computed value yet, THE parleyd SHALL store conflict and the conflict report on the change and write one parley.change.conflict event in the same transaction
   → GET returns mergeable 'conflict' and a conflict object whose files list has one entry per conflicted path; one event parley.change.conflict with actor system, resource_type change, resource_id the number, the target workspace, and metadata number, ref, version, head_sha, files (the conflicted paths) and needs_restack (the change's current flag)
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()

   - setup: open change demo#1 with mergeable clean, editing line 1 of a.txt

   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] WHILE the last computed mergeable value of a change is conflict, THE parleyd SHALL on each further computation that finds a conflict, for the same or a later version or target head, replace the stored conflict report and write no event
   → after a new version that still conflicts and after a further target move that still conflicts, the count of parley.change.conflict events for the change is still 1 and conflict.target_sha and conflict.head_sha are those of the latest computation

1. [REQ-8.3] WHEN a computation finds clean for a change whose stored mergeable value was conflict, THE parleyd SHALL store clean and clear the conflict report in one transaction, so that a later conflict is announced again

1. [REQ-8.4] WHEN a mergeability result, a move from draft to open, a retarget or a restore leaves a change open with landing.status ready and mergeable clean, for a head_sha for which the change has not been announced since it last was not landable, THE parleyd SHALL write one parley.change.ready event in the same transaction that makes the change landable and remember the announced head
   → one event parley.change.ready with actor system, resource_type change, resource_id the number, the target workspace and metadata number, ref, version and head_sha, and no further metadata

   - setup: no policy set on the workspace, so landing.status is ready for every open change with commits to land

### REQ-9: Reconcile changes with their source branches at start

**Rationale:** A crash between a ref update and its bookkeeping must not lose a version.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-9.1] WHEN parleyd starts and the source branch of a draft or open change points at a commit other than the head of the change's current version, THE parleyd SHALL record that commit as a new version of kind ref (the kind of every version recorded for a head that was already on the source branch) with created_by.actor_type system and no creating credential, through the version recording of package 22 with everything a new version brings, before the listener accepts a request
   → the first GET after start returns the change with version one higher and head_sha equal to the branch head; refs/parley/changes/<number>/<new version> resolves to it; one parley.change.version event with actor system and kind 'ref' exists for the new version
   Check: integration
   - setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 against a store and a repository directory in t.TempDir()
   - setup: workspace 'demo' owned by user owner, with branch main and an org member user 'mia' who has a fork 'demo--t1'
   - setup: open change demo#1 with one version; the hub can be stopped and started again on the same store and repositories

   ```
1. [REQ-9.2] WHILE the source branch of every draft or open change points at the head of its current version when parleyd starts, THE parleyd SHALL record no version, write no event and leave updated_at of every change as it was
   → after two restarts in a row every change has the same version, head_sha and updated_at as before, and the event log has the same length

   ```

[REQ-9.5] IF reconciling one change fails because its source or target repository cannot be read or the version cannot be recorded, THEN THE parleyd SHALL log the failure with the workspace slug and the change number, leave that change as it was, reconcile the remaining changes and finish the start

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An agent finishes a draft, marks it ready and waits until it is landable

1. **agent** pushes a branch to its fork with git and opens a draft change into main of the parent with an empty intent
2. **parley CLI** runs `parley change edit demo 1 --intent "why" --label area:api`, reading the change and sending PATCH with intent and labels
3. **parleyd** checks that the caller is the change's author, stores intent and labels and answers 200 with the change object
4. **parley CLI** runs `parley change ready demo 1`, sending PATCH with state open
5. **parleyd** moves the change to open, re-evaluates landing and writes parley.change.open with was_draft true
6. **parleyd** trial-rebases the change onto the head of main in the background, stores mergeable clean and writes parley.change.ready
7. **parley CLI** runs `parley change wait demo 1 --for ready`, polls the change and exits 0 with the change on stdout

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the net/http router, middleware and error envelope of internal/server, authentication of internal/identity and the access rule of internal/access, the change store, routes and mergeability worker of internal/change, the event log of internal/event, the git binary through internal/gitrepo on bare repositories on disk, the SQLite store of internal/store, the parley CLI of internal/cli run in-process against the hub's address, a stock git client pushing over the git server of internal/gitserver

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with store and repositories in t.TempDir() and [changes].mergeable_debounce = "0s"
- workspace 'demo' with branch main seeded by a real git push; org member mia with fork 'demo--t1' and a PAT bound to it with changes:read and changes:write; the workspace owner with an API key
- no policy set on the workspace

**End state:**

- the change is open with intent 'why', labels ['area:api'], landing.status ready and mergeable clean
- the event log holds, for the change, parley.change.version (version 1, draft true), then parley.change.open (was_draft true), then exactly one parley.change.ready
- `parley change wait --for ready` exited 0 and printed the change

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/change_lifecycle_test.go: git push the branch to the fork with mia's bound token; open the draft with POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes {source:{workspace_slug:'demo--t1',branch:'feat'}, draft:true}; cli('change','edit','demo','1','--intent','why','--label','area:api') exits 0; cli('change','ready','demo','1') exits 0 and prints state 'open'; out, code = cli('change','wait','demo','1','--for','ready','--timeout','20s','--poll-interval','100ms'); assert code == 0 and out.mergeable == 'clean' and out.landing.status == 'ready'; types = event types for change 1 in seq order; assert types == ['parley.change.version','parley.change.open','parley.change.ready']
```

### PATH-2: A target move makes an open change conflict and a new version clears it

1. **agent** has an open change from its fork into main that edits a line of a.txt, with mergeable clean
2. **developer** pushes to main, as the workspace owner, a commit that edits the same line of a.txt
3. **git client** sends the push over smart HTTP and receives the accepted ref update
4. **parleyd** sets mergeable to unknown on every draft and open change that targets main and schedules their checks
5. **parleyd** trial-rebases the change onto the new head of main, stores mergeable conflict with the conflict report and writes one parley.change.conflict naming a.txt
6. **agent** rebases its branch onto main, resolves a.txt and force-pushes the branch to its fork
7. **parleyd** records the new version, recomputes, stores mergeable clean, clears the conflict report and writes parley.change.ready for the new head

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the net/http router, middleware and error envelope of internal/server, authentication of internal/identity and the access rule of internal/access, the change store, routes and mergeability worker of internal/change, the event log of internal/event, the git binary through internal/gitrepo on bare repositories on disk, the SQLite store of internal/store, a stock git client pushing over the git server of internal/gitserver, with the push rules of package 18 and the version recording of package 22

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with store and repositories in t.TempDir() and [changes].mergeable_debounce = "0s"
- workspace 'demo' with branch main seeded by a real git push; org member mia with fork 'demo--t1' and a PAT bound to it with changes:read and changes:write; the workspace owner with an API key
- no policy set on the workspace
- open change demo#1 from branch 'feat' of demo--t1 editing line 1 of a.txt, already announced with one parley.change.ready

**End state:**

- after the owner's push the change is open with mergeable conflict and conflict.files names a.txt, and exactly one parley.change.conflict event exists
- after the agent's force push the change has version 2, mergeable clean and conflict null
- two parley.change.ready events exist for the change, the second with the head_sha of version 2
- main still points at the owner's commit and the fork's branch at the agent's pushed commit: no check moved a ref

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/change_lifecycle_test.go: owner clones demo, edits line 1 of a.txt, git push origin main; poll GET change until mergeable != 'unknown'; assert mergeable == 'conflict' and conflict.files[0].path == 'a.txt'; assert count(parley.change.conflict) == 1 and its metadata.files == ['a.txt']; mia: git fetch, git rebase origin/main with the resolution, git push --force to the fork; poll until version == 2 and mergeable != 'unknown'; assert mergeable == 'clean' and conflict == null; ready = events parley.change.ready; assert len(ready) == 2 and ready[1].metadata.head_sha == change.head_sha; assert git ls-remote of main and of the fork branch equal the pushed commits
```

### PATH-3: A developer abandons a change, deletes its branch and restores it

1. **developer** runs `parley change abandon demo 1 --reason "parked"` on an open change whose source is a branch of demo itself
2. **parley CLI** sends POST …/changes/1/abandon with the reason and prints the change
3. **parleyd** moves the change to abandoned, keeps the source branch and the version refs, and writes parley.change.abandon with reason parked
4. **git client** deletes the source branch with `git push origin --delete feat`, which is accepted because no draft or open change uses the branch
5. **developer** runs `parley change restore demo 1`
6. **parleyd** recreates the source branch at the last version's head, moves the change to open, writes parley.change.restore and schedules the mergeability check
7. **parleyd** stores mergeable clean and writes parley.change.ready

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the net/http router, middleware and error envelope of internal/server, authentication of internal/identity and the access rule of internal/access, the change store, routes and mergeability worker of internal/change, the event log of internal/event, the git binary through internal/gitrepo on bare repositories on disk, the SQLite store of internal/store, the parley CLI of internal/cli run in-process against the hub's address, a stock git client pushing over the git server of internal/gitserver

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with store and repositories in t.TempDir() and [changes].mergeable_debounce = "0s"
- workspace 'demo' with branch main seeded by a real git push; org member mia with fork 'demo--t1' and a PAT bound to it with changes:read and changes:write; the workspace owner with an API key
- no policy set on the workspace
- open change demo#2 opened by the owner from branch 'feat' of demo into main, with two versions

**End state:**

- after the abandon: state abandoned, branch feat and refs/parley/changes/2/1 and /2/2 still present
- after the restore: state open at version 2, branch feat exists again at the head of version 2, mergeable clean
- the event log holds parley.change.abandon (reason 'parked') and parley.change.restore for the change, and no parley.change.open after the restore
- a second `parley change restore demo 2` exits 1 with error_type change_not_abandoned

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/change_lifecycle_test.go: out, code = cli('change','abandon','demo','2','--reason','parked'); assert code == 0 and out.state == 'abandoned'; assert git ls-remote lists refs/heads/feat and refs/parley/changes/2/2; git push origin --delete feat succeeds; assert GET change is still abandoned; out, code = cli('change','restore','demo','2'); assert code == 0 and out.state == 'open' and out.version == 2; assert git ls-remote refs/heads/feat == out.head_sha; poll until mergeable == 'clean'; assert event types for change 2 after the abandon call == ['parley.change.abandon','parley.change.restore','parley.change.ready']; _, code, err = cli('change','restore','demo','2'); assert code == 1 and err.error.error_type == 'change_not_abandoned'
```

### PATH-4: A restart records a head whose bookkeeping was lost

1. **agent** has an open change from its fork with one version
2. **operator** stops parleyd; the source branch then moves in the fork's repository without a version being recorded, as after a crash between a ref update and its bookkeeping
3. **operator** starts parleyd again on the same data directory
4. **parleyd** compares each draft and open change's current version with its source branch head before listening, records the differing head as version 2 of kind ref and writes parley.change.version
5. **parleyd** starts listening, computes mergeability for the new head and stores the result
6. **agent** reads the change and finds version 2 at the branch head with a computed mergeable value

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the net/http router, middleware and error envelope of internal/server, authentication of internal/identity and the access rule of internal/access, the change store, routes and mergeability worker of internal/change, the event log of internal/event, the git binary through internal/gitrepo on bare repositories on disk, the SQLite store of internal/store, the start-up sequence of internal/hub/change.go run twice on the same data directory

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with store and repositories in t.TempDir() and [changes].mergeable_debounce = "0s"
- workspace 'demo' with branch main seeded by a real git push; org member mia with fork 'demo--t1' and a PAT bound to it with changes:read and changes:write; the workspace owner with an API key
- no policy set on the workspace
- open change demo#1 from branch 'feat' of demo--t1 with one version

**End state:**

- the first GET after the second start returns version 2 with head_sha equal to the moved branch head
- refs/parley/changes/1/2 resolves to that head in demo
- the versions list ends with a version of kind ref created by actor_type system
- mergeable is clean without any push or request other than reads
- a third start records no further version

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/change_lifecycle_test.go: stop the hub; in the fork's bare repository create a commit on top of feat with git commit-tree and git update-ref refs/heads/feat; start the hub on the same directories; c = GET change; assert c.version == 2 and c.head_sha == the new commit; assert git ls-remote refs/parley/changes/1/2 == the new commit; v = GET versions; assert v[-1].kind == 'ref' and v[-1].created_by.actor_type == 'system'; poll until c.mergeable == 'clean'; stop and start again; assert GET change .version == 2
```

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/change/... ./internal/cli/... ./internal/config/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `09` — builds its CLI commands on the client, output and exit-code helpers of the CLI foundation
- `12` — registers with its branch-move observer to learn of target branches a sync moved
- `18` — registers a ref-updated stage with its ref writer to learn of moved and deleted target branches
- `22` — edits, abandons and restores the change record package 22 defines, and uses its version recording, version observers, StackLinker and ForkActivity interfaces, target validation, landing re-evaluation and read route
- `52` — emits its hub events through the event log component

## Tasks

### 1. Register the three write routes behind the caller rule (implement)

- 1.3 After the access step, load the change by workspace and number; answer 404 change_not_found for a :number that is not a positive decimal integer, for a number with no change, and, when the caller's token is bound to a fork and the addressed workspace is that fork's parent, for a change whose source workspace is not that fork (use the same confinement package 22 applies to its read routes)
- 1.4 Add one function that decides whether a caller may modify a change: true for the admin token, for a caller whose access level on the target workspace allows writes, and for a caller whose user id equals the change's author.actor_id whatever the credential; answer 403 forbidden with the change untouched otherwise
- 1.5 Add one function that maps the target workspace's status to the refusal of WS-FR-007 (pending, cloning or running maintenance: 409 workspace_busy; failed: 409 workspace_not_ready; archived: 409 workspace_archived) and call it in each handler after body validation and before any state check of the change
- 1.6 Have each handler run, in this order, the caller rule, the body decoding and validation, the workspace status check and then its operation. In this task the edit operation stores labels only, abandon handles a change without dependants and restore handles a change whose source branch is at its last version's head; tasks 2 and 5 to 8 complete the operations

### 3. Run mergeability checks in a background worker (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7

**Depends on:** 1

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the mergeability behaviours to internal/change/mergeable_test.go on real bare repositories made with git in t.TempDir(), and the configuration behaviours to internal/config/config_test.go, and confirm they fail
- 3.2 Read [changes].mergeable_debounce in internal/config: a duration, default 5s when the key or the table is absent, 0s allowed; a negative or unparsable value is a load error whose text names changes.mergeable_debounce, which stops parleyd before it listens
- 3.3 Store on the change, beside mergeable, the pair of commits (head and onto-commit) the value was computed for and the last computed value (a schema migration registered with internal/store)
- 3.4 Add the worker: a per-change pending set so that any number of triggers for one change leaves one pending entry; a per-change earliest-next-start time of last start plus the debounce; a small fixed pool of goroutines; an injectable clock, trial-rebase function and deadline for tests; a stop that waits for running computations when the server shuts down
- 3.5 Add the trigger entry points and connect them: register a version observer with package 22 (a version recorded for a draft or open change triggers that change and the draft or open changes that depend on it, whatever recorded the version, a restack of package 24 included); register a ref-updated stage with the ref writer of package 18 (RegisterRefUpdatedStage) that triggers the draft and open changes whose target is a branch a push, an API write or a land moved or deleted, and the branch-move observer of package 12 for a sync; export triggers for retarget, for restore and for package 24 (a needs_restack flag cleared without a new version). Each sets mergeable to unknown in the triggering transaction and adds the change to the pending set after commit
- 3.6 Compute: read the change's current head, base and onto-commit at computation start (the target branch head, or the head of the depends_on change when that change is draft or open); run the trial rebase of internal/gitrepo (package 20, which returns the one ConflictReport type on a conflict) for base..head onto the onto-commit under a 30 second deadline; write no ref and leave no worktree or temporary ref
- 3.7 Store the result only when the change is still draft or open and its head and onto-commit are still the ones computed; otherwise discard it and leave the change pending for the newer pair
- 3.8 When the target branch does not exist: leave unknown, clear nothing else, and run the landing re-evaluation of package 22 so that landing reports blocked with reason target_not_found
- 3.9 When the trial rebase returns a non-conflict error or passes its deadline: cancel the git process, leave unknown, log the workspace slug and change number, and go on with other changes
- 3.10 Start the worker from internal/hub/change.go with the configured debounce and stop it on shutdown
